passage:
Nitin, notes for tomorrow when you babysit Juhi.
Today at the park she asked for a second ice lolly. I said no.
First came crying, big tears, peeking at me between sobs.
Then promises: "I'll sleep early, I'll eat all my dal, pinky promise!"
When that didn't work, she shouted so loudly the whole bench turned around.
Each time she stopped and checked my face.
I nearly caved at the shouting part. I didn't.
If she gets the lolly after screaming, tomorrow she'll scream sooner.
So please: kind voice, same answer. 🙏
- Varun

qa.q: What did Juhi promise when the crying didn't work?
qa.a: She promised, "I'll sleep early, I'll eat all my dal, pinky promise!"

qa.q: Why did Juhi keep stopping to check Varun's face?
qa.a: Juhi was hopeful the no might move; each pause shows her watching to see if crying, promising or shouting was starting to work.

qa.q: What turning point does Varun's note point to at this stage?
qa.a: Keeping the same answer even through the loudest shouting, so Juhi learns that tantrums don't shift limits and the pattern fades instead of growing.

qa.q: What would tomorrow be like for Nitin if he hands Juhi a lolly after a scream?
qa.a: Nitin would get a quick moment of quiet, but Juhi would learn that screaming works and try it sooner and louder, making the day harder.

grounding: A caregiver's note records a five-year-old girl moving from crying to promising to shouting while watching whether the limit will move.

passage: The weekly haat at Rangpo was loud with bargaining. Pema, five, stopped at a stall of tin whistles. "Papa, buy one!" Her father, Varun, said, "Not today, we came for rice." Pema's lip trembled and she cried loudly, one eye open, watching him. He kept walking. She ran after him. "I'll carry the bag! I'll never ask again!" He shook his head gently. Then she stood in the mud and shouted, so loudly the vegetable seller laughed. Varun felt every face turn. His hand went to his pocket, then stopped. "Still no, Pema," he said, and held out his hand.

qa.q: What had Pema and Varun come to the haat to buy?
qa.a: They came for rice.

qa.q: What does Pema crying with one eye open suggest about what she wants?
qa.a: She wants the tin whistle and is checking whether her tears are moving her father; the crying is partly a test of the limit, not only sadness.

qa.q: What is the turning point in this scene, and why does it matter?
qa.a: It is the moment Varun's hand goes to his pocket and stops; by holding the no through the shouting, he keeps Pema from learning that a louder tantrum wins.

qa.q: What is Varun going through as the vegetable seller laughs?
qa.a: He feels embarrassed with every face turned his way and tempted to buy the whistle just to end it, which makes staying calm harder.

grounding: Shows a young girl trying crying, promising and then shouting while testing whether her father's no will give way.

passage:
The billing queue was long and the air conditioner was broken. Rashmi had eleven minutes before the school van dropped Kashish's brother home.
At the counter, Kashish grabbed a lollipop. "Please, Mumma?"
"Not today."
Kashish's eyes filled. She peeked through her fingers at Rashmi's face. No change. "I'll eat all my dal. I promise, I promise!" Another peek. Still no. Then she shouted, so loudly that the man behind them sighed.
Rashmi's cheeks burned. She tossed the lollipop onto the belt. "Fine. Just be quiet."
Kashish stopped at once and smiled.

qa.q: How many minutes did Rashmi have before the school van came?
qa.a: Eleven minutes.

qa.q: What does Kashish peeking through her fingers suggest she was thinking?
qa.a: She was hopeful and watchful, checking whether crying or promising was working before trying something bigger.

qa.q: What turning point is available to Rashmi at this stage?
qa.a: She could hold the no calmly even with people watching, so Kashish learns that shouting does not move the limit.

qa.q: How is Rashmi experiencing the queue at this moment?
qa.a: She feels rushed and embarrassed with strangers sighing, which makes giving in feel like the quickest way out.

grounding: Shows a girl trying crying, promising and then shouting while watching her mother, who gives in, so the tantrum works.

passage:
Outside the colony kirana shop, Aditi pointed at the jar of orange toffees. "One, Dadi?"
Vasudha Dadi shook her head. "We came for milk only."
Aditi's face crumpled and she cried, loud and wet. Between sobs she looked up to check. Dadi was counting coins.
"I'll sleep early! I'll brush my teeth two times!"
Dadi smiled but shook her head again. "Still no, chinni."
Aditi stamped and shouted, "You never give me anything!" Then she stopped to see what would happen.
Dadi picked up the milk packet and held out her hand. After a long moment, Aditi took it.

qa.q: What did Vasudha Dadi say they came to the shop for?
qa.a: Milk only.

qa.q: Why did Aditi stop shouting to see what would happen?
qa.a: She was testing, curious and hopeful that the shouting might finally change Dadi's answer, and uncertain when it did not.

qa.q: Which of Dadi's choices worked at this stage, and why?
qa.a: She kept the same calm no through crying, promises and shouting, so Aditi saw that none of them moved the limit.

qa.q: What is it like for Vasudha Dadi to hold the line outside a busy shop?
qa.a: She may feel tender towards Aditi and a bit tired, yet steady, since she smiles while still saying no.

grounding: Shows a girl trying crying, promising and shouting while watching whether her grandmother's limit will move, and it does not.

passage:
"Aadhya didi, can I have ice cream?"
"Your Abbu said no sweets before dinner, Hafsa."
"But I'm sooo sad." A big sniff. Hafsa watched Aadhya's face.
"I can see you're sad."
"If I get ice cream I'll tidy all my blocks. Every single one."
"That's a kind offer. Still no ice cream before dinner."
"You're the worst babysitter EVER!" Hafsa shouted, then glanced at the freezer.
"You can shout, and it's still no. Want to help me set the table instead?"
Hafsa folded her arms. "...Can I do the spoons?"

qa.q: What did Hafsa promise to do if she got ice cream?
qa.a: She promised she would tidy all her blocks, every single one.

qa.q: Why did Hafsa glance at the freezer after shouting?
qa.a: She was hopeful and watchful, checking whether the shout had worked after crying and promising had not.

qa.q: What went well in how Aadhya answered, and why does it matter at this stage?
qa.a: Aadhya named Hafsa's sadness but kept the same no each time, so Hafsa learns that shouting does not change limits.

qa.q: How might Aadhya feel while Hafsa tries every trick?
qa.a: Probably a little tested and uneasy, as a babysitter wanting to be liked, but calm enough to offer a job instead.

grounding: Shows a girl trying crying, promising and shouting while checking whether the babysitter's limit will move.

passage: Teacher's note, Nursery B, Monday. At tidy-up, Deepika wanted more time with the clay. First she cried. When I said, "Tidy-up time now," she tried promising: "Just two minutes, I'll tidy everything, I promise!" Then she watched my face very carefully. When I said no again, she shouted, "You're mean!" and looked to see what I would do. Last week a helper gave in to her, and I think she remembers. Today I kept the same calm words and helped her put the clay away. Irfan, beside her, watched the whole thing. Tomorrow I'll give a five-minute warning before tidy-up.

qa.q: What did Deepika want more time with?
qa.a: She wanted more time with the clay.

qa.q: Why did Deepika watch the teacher's face so carefully?
qa.a: She was testing, hopeful that promising or shouting might move the limit, as it had when a helper gave in last week.

qa.q: Why does keeping the same calm answer matter now?
qa.a: If the limit moves after crying or shouting, Deepika learns that tantrums work; staying calm and consistent teaches her they don't.

qa.q: What might Irfan be learning as he watches?
qa.a: Irfan may feel curious and a bit unsettled, and he also sees that shouting did not change the rule.

grounding: Shows a young child cycling through crying, promising and shouting while watching to see whether the limit will move.
